activity.notes: Matilda of Tuscany (Matilda of Canossa) became the principal holder and governor of the vast Canossa dynastic dominions after the death of her mother Beatrice in 1076 and remained the central political authority of those lands until her death in 1115. Her territories were a heterogeneous feudal complex extending across parts of northern and central Italy, and imperial action in the Investiture Controversy repeatedly challenged her legal rights and effective control. ATLAS therefore uses the map-level polity Canossa Dominions with governs + de_facto_rule rather than pretending that her authority was an uninterrupted modern territorial state or reducing it only to the later geographical label Tuscany.

sources.title: Matilda of Canossa — Treccani, Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani
sources.citation_text: Treccani notes that after Beatrice's death in 1076 Matilda bore the burden of governing her vast and articulated territories and remained a major political actor until her death in 1115.

sources.title: Matilda of Canossa — Treccani
sources.citation_text: Treccani describes Matilda as daughter of the Margrave of Tuscany and holder of extensive dominions in northern and central Italy.
